ii.answer: people buying Instax / instant cameras // people buying film / analogue cameras
ii.notes: Accept buyers of Instax/instant cameras or, more generally, people buying film/analogue cameras. Reject 'students' alone.

6.answer: Although he does not understand why young people pay for film but only look at it on their phones, he is happy to take their money // their custom is good for his shop.
6.notes: Must show the idea that he accepts / welcomes the customers' money despite not understanding (or not agreeing with) their behaviour. Accept any reasonable answer.
reject: copying 'I don’t get it, but business is business' without explanation

v.notes: Spelling must be correct; 'scan' is not accepted (plural needed).

10.answer: They cannot see the photo until it has been developed, so they cannot choose / edit / improve it before other people see it.
10.notes: Must convey that the photographer has not seen the picture either (no chance to check/select/edit). Accept any reasonable paraphrase.
reject: copying 'because, well, you haven’t seen it either' without explanation

12.answer: The (very high) prices of / demand for old cameras will suddenly fall // the trend will suddenly end (and he will not be able to sell his cameras).
12.notes: Must show a sudden collapse/end of the high demand or prices. A literal answer about a soap bubble scores 0.

para 9: cleaned, tested and repaired 'before being listed' in his online shop

para 10: an expense that, Mr Kwok grumbles, keeps rising

15.answer: that film photographers remember (things / events) more // that taking film photos helps them remember better
15.notes: Must refer to remembering more. 'The camera' or 'the study' scores 0.

vocab.clue: para 12: 'settling into a small but loyal market'

17.answer: He has already seen film (almost) die once, so he knows demand can collapse again // he will be fine whatever happens (he will retire or carry on).
17.notes: Either reason is acceptable. Must show understanding; copying 'I’ve seen film die once already' alone is acceptable only if linked to the possibility of it happening again.

accept: to handle film without a darkroom

31.answer: The authorities / the government know(s) about the shortage in advance (because the union warns them) but pretend(s) not to // do(es) nothing about it.
31.notes: Must show the idea that they already know but behave as if they did not / fail to act. 'They are surprised' scores 0.
reject: the government is surprised every year

33.notes: Both letters must be correct for the mark.

34.answer: (working as) a lifeguard // the lifeguard job // lifeguarding

vocab.clue: para 2: teenagers 'would jump at the chance to earn some money'

39.notes: Answer must be an adverb that fits 'train very ____'. Idiom: 'put us through our paces'.

40.answer: Because it supplied the pool with trained lifeguards every summer // it helped the pool solve its staff shortage (it 'saved' the pool).
40.notes: Must link the club to providing staff/lifeguards to the pool. Literal answers about a rope score 0.

points.answer: they would earn money // they would do something useful (outdoors) instead of staring at their phones
it would help solve the lifeguard shortage // some would stay on as lifeguards for years

42.notes: Point 1 must be a benefit for teenagers; point 2 a benefit for pools. Accept any reasonable wording. 'Classes would not be cancelled' may be tolerated for point 2.

47.answer: Because the apps make money from advertisers, who pay for users’ attention // users are not the customers; their attention is what is sold.
47.notes: Must mention advertisers paying / attention being sold. 'Because they want more users' scores 0.

49.notes: Must be an adjective; 'unpredictably' is grammatically incorrect.

50.answer: (the number of) daily active users // a three per cent increase in daily active users

51.answer: An unpredictable / surprise reward (like a slot machine): the delay makes the ‘like’ feel like a surprise, which keeps people coming back.
51.notes: Must identify the unpredictable / surprise reward principle (slot machine, pull-to-refresh, Skinner’s pigeons). Accept 'a surprise reward that keeps people checking, like a slot machine'. 'It makes it a surprise' alone, with no link to the reward technique, scores 0.

52.answer: Designers only see numbers / data (graphs), not the real people affected by their decisions, so they do not feel the harm they cause.
52.notes: Must contrast data/graphs with real people/users.
reject: designers do not meet each other

53.answer: To show that, unlike apps, potatoes are not deliberately designed to make us consume more, so the potato comparison misses the question of design.
53.notes: Must convey the contrast: apps are deliberately engineered / designed to hold us; potatoes are not. Answers that only repeat that the effect is small score 0.

points.answer: ‘worn away by the weather’: a natural / gradual process that nobody is responsible for (nobody is to blame).
‘mined’: attention has been deliberately taken / extracted by companies for profit.

57.notes: One mark for each image. Answers must interpret the image, not repeat it.

58.answer: (the) shrinking (of) attention spans // attention spans shrinking
58.notes: Accept 'attention spans shrinking (is not) a natural process'. 'Attention (spans)' alone, 'a natural process', 'coastal erosion' or 'the weather' scores 0.

59.answer: Abara’s umbrellas are regulations made by others (governments), whereas the writer’s is a personal measure she chose herself – an alarm clock, so that her phone spends the night in the kitchen.
59.notes: Must contrast regulations by others with the writer’s own personal measure (the alarm clock). Naming only the alarm clock scores 0.

60.answer: To show that even though she understands how apps work (and has taken steps against them), she still cannot resist her phone // she is still being manipulated, just like at the start of the essay.
60.notes: Must show the irony that knowledge / her small umbrella has not freed her. Accept link back to paragraph 1, or the irony that by doubting the figure she does what the app wants.

v.answer: slot machines // a slot machine // the casino

62.answer: The commenter is referring to the video the writer watched in paragraph 1 and suggesting that the writer may simply have enjoyed it – not everything people do on their phones is the result of manipulation.
62.notes: Must show the link to the writer’s own knife video OR the idea that people use phones because they genuinely enjoy it, not because they are manipulated.
